$comment: Leader Archetype content layer v2 (13 Aug 2026). Maps 1:1 onto profile numbers 1-8 in archetype-schema.json. Copy sourced from leaderarchetypesvWORKING.pptx with typos normalised; Australian English. This file is presentation copy only; it must never affect scoring.

archetypes.name: The Innovator
archetypes.essence: Can't stop inventing; finds the best ideas where others would have given up.
archetypes.description: Innovators can't stop themselves from thinking up new things. They often find their best ideas when others would have given up. Before Thomas Edison's light bulb succeeded he had many failures, but his persistence paid off.

archetypes.name: The Influencer
archetypes.essence: Thrives in the spotlight; natural charm that draws people in.
archetypes.description: Influencers thrive in the spotlight. They adapt quickly and have a natural charm that draws people in. Their confidence is inspiring, like Oprah Winfrey, who turned her media presence into a global brand.
watchouts: Not spending time with the team

archetypes.name: The Guide
archetypes.essence: Motivates and directs; turns information into action.
archetypes.description: Guides excel at motivating and directing people. They turn information into action and are excellent at rallying their teams, similar to how Nelson Mandela led with vision and compassion.

archetypes.name: The Negotiator
archetypes.essence: Finds the best deals; brings people together for mutual benefit.
archetypes.description: Negotiators are skilled at finding the best deals and bringing people together for mutual benefit. They are charismatic and excel at reading situations, much like Warren Buffett in the investment world.
watchouts: Risk of being seen as a manipulator

archetypes.name: The Play Maker
archetypes.essence: Reads the market; times the moves that maximise returns.
archetypes.description: Play Makers are experts at identifying the right time to buy and sell assets. They analyse markets and trends to maximise their profits, like George Soros, who made billions through strategic trades.

archetypes.name: The Architect
archetypes.description: Architects focus on gradually accumulating assets. They are patient and thorough, ensuring that their investments grow over time, similar to how Warren Buffett built his fortune.

archetypes.name: The Guardian
archetypes.essence: Meticulous with resources; consistent cash flow, controlled risk.
archetypes.description: Guardians are meticulous in managing resources and ensuring consistent cash flow. They are detail-oriented and avoid unnecessary risks, like John D. Rockefeller, who dominated the oil industry through careful management.

archetypes.name: The Engineer
archetypes.essence: Refines systems; always tinkering toward a better way.
archetypes.description: Engineers are focused on improving and refining systems. They love to tinker and find better ways to do things, much like Henry Ford revolutionised automobile manufacturing.
